glossary.def: Observed error rate divided by the error budget (1 minus the SLO). A burn rate of 1 spends exactly the budget over the SLO window.
The share of events allowed to be bad under an SLO, for example 0.1 percent for 99.9 percent. Alerts fire when it is spent too fast.
Scoring a sample of live traces with reference-free judges and safety checks, because production runs have no reference answers.
Foundry trace selection that dedupes, filters broken traces and picks diverse ones with MinHash farthest-first, with no extra model calls (preview).
The MCP request field that carries `traceparent`, `tracestate` and `baggage` so a tool call joins the caller's trace.
The OTel GenAI span for a graph or orchestrator that coordinates several agents. It is INTERNAL and not used for a standalone agent.
The Application Insights field that says how many original items a retained, sampled item stands for. Weight sums by it.
A standalone local OpenTelemetry viewer run in Docker. Agent Framework docs use OTLP port 4317 and UI port 18888. For development only.
An evaluator that needs no ground-truth answer, such as an LLM judge for groundedness or a safety classifier.
An agent run with an abnormal number of model or tool calls. Detect it with `gen_ai.invoke_agent.inference_calls` and `.tool_calls`.

claims.text: All OpenTelemetry GenAI conventions have status Development as of 2026-10-13, and the docs moved to open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai on 2026-05-05 (PR 3696).
v1.41.1 (2026-05-11) of the old conventions repository still holds the full GenAI docs, while v1.42.0 (2026-06-12) holds only a Moved stub.
gen_ai.operation.name and gen_ai.provider.name are required on inference spans.

The v1.41 conventions defined a gen_ai.client.token.usage histogram, the new repository defines gen_ai.client.inference.usage.* counters, and Agent Framework docs still list gen_ai.client.token.usage.

Inference spans are named {gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model} with kind CLIENT, invoke_agent is CLIENT for remote services and INTERNAL in-process, and execute_tool and invoke_workflow are INTERNAL.
Agent Framework emits the spans invoke_agent <agent_name>, chat <model_name> and execute_tool <function_name>.
Agent Framework workflow spans include workflow.build, workflow.session or workflow.run, workflow_invoke, executor.process, edge_group.process and message.send.
In .NET, gen_ai spans appear only after wrapping with UseOpenTelemetry, and wrapping both the client and the agent duplicates content when sensitive data is on.
gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens includes cached tokens and .output_tokens includes reasoning tokens, with subset counters for cache read, cache write and reasoning.
The per-operation token histograms should not be used for total usage or cost calculations.
gen_ai.client.inference.duration and time_to_first_chunk are histograms in seconds with explicit buckets from 0.01 doubling to 81.92, and time_to_first_chunk applies to streaming only.
API Management llm-emit-token-metric allows up to five custom dimensions, 100 unique values per dimension and 1,000 active time series per namespace, and drops the excess silently.
Interrupted streams give wrong token counts in API Management, some OpenAI streams need include_usage set to true, and cached and reasoning categories are in preview.

The W3C traceparent header has the form 00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex parent id>-<2 hex flags>, Trace Context Level 1 is a Recommendation (2021-11-23) and Level 2 is a Candidate Recommendation Draft (2024-03-28).
The conventions inject traceparent, tracestate and baggage into MCP params._meta with unprefixed keys, and MCP 2026-07-28 reserves those keys.
Agent Framework Python injects W3C trace context into params._meta for MCP sessions it opens itself, but not for hosted or provider-managed MCP tools, and .NET behavior is unverified.
A2A defines no tracing fields, and its enterprise guidance says to propagate W3C Trace Context over HTTP and to log taskId, sessionId and correlation ids.
OpenTelemetry baggage is propagated across service boundaries and to third-party APIs, so sensitive information must not be placed in it.
The GenAI conventions say instrumentations SHOULD NOT capture content by default and recommend storing content externally with references on spans for production.
Agent Framework ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA defaults to false and covers prompts, responses, tool arguments and tool results.
The @trace_function decorator always records parameters and return values regardless of the content recording flag.
OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true enables content recording in Foundry, and the older classic page used AZURE_TRACING_GEN_AI_CONTENT_RECORDING_ENABLED.
Head sampling decides early and cannot guarantee keeping error traces, while tail sampling decides after the trace is complete and needs a stateful collector.

The Microsoft OpenTelemetry Distro defaults to rate-limited sampling at five traces per second for Azure Monitor export, Python uses OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER and OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, and metrics are not sampled.
The Foundry portal Traces tab shows 90 days of traces.
Foundry server-side tracing turns on after connecting Application Insights, is GA for prompt and hosted agents and preview for workflow and external agents, and client-side tracing is preview.
Client-side Foundry tracing needs AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING=true (Python) or the Azure.Experimental.EnableGenAITracing switch (.NET) set before creating the client.
The Application Insights Agents (Preview) view relies on gen_ai.usage.input_tokens and gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, and spans land in the dependencies table with attributes in customDimensions.
Agent Framework Python instrumentation became on by default in python-1.6.0 (2026-05-21), and no exporter is installed automatically.
Agent Framework Python defaults: ENABLE_INSTRUMENTATION true, ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA false, ENABLE_CONSOLE_EXPORTERS false, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME agent_framework and OTLP protocol grpc.
The .NET default source name is Experimental.Microsoft.Agents.AI, the tracer and meter providers must AddSource the same name, and the Harness wraps both layers by default.
The SRE Workbook recommends paging at 2 percent budget in 1 hour (burn rate 14.4) and 5 percent in 6 hours (burn rate 6), and a ticket at 10 percent in 3 days (burn rate 1).
The SRE Workbook suggests making the short alert window one twelfth of the long window.
Foundry continuous evaluation is preview, has a documented default of 100 runs per hour (max_hourly_runs) after which runs are skipped, and needs Foundry User on the project managed identity.
Foundry intelligent sampling does exact dedupe, hard filters, aggregation and MinHash farthest-first selection on local compute with no extra model calls.
LangSmith online evaluations run on production runs without reference outputs, with sampling rate, filters and spend limits set per attached project or dataset.
Langfuse accepts OTLP at /api/public/otel over HTTP/JSON or HTTP/protobuf and does not support gRPC.
LangSmith's OTLP endpoint is https://api.smith.langchain.com/otel with an x-api-key header, and adding /v1/traces to the base endpoint returns 404.
Arize Phoenix is built on OpenTelemetry and powered by OpenInference instrumentation.
